# Tidewater Dispatch: H2 2026 Roadmap

## 1. Scored backlog

**Formulas**
- **Normalised effort (eng-wks)** = stated effort, converted to engineer-weeks. F7 was submitted in engineer-days, so 45 ÷ 5 = **9**. All other items are already in weeks.
- **Value (R×I×C)** = Reach × Impact × Confidence. This is the total benefit before effort is considered. I use it to compare bundles of items that compete for the same capacity.
- **RICE** = Reach × Impact × Confidence ÷ Normalised effort.

**Scored items (discretionary)**

| ID | Item | Reach | Impact | Confidence | Effort (as submitted) | Normalised effort (eng-wks) | Value (R×I×C) | RICE | Rank |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| F6 | Invoice PDF redesign | 600 | 0.5 | 90% | 3 wks | 3 | 270 | **90.0** | 1 |
| F1 | Offline mode (mobile) | 420 | 2 | 80% | 16 wks | 16 | 672 | **42.0** | 2 |
| F7 | Technician skills matching | 250 | 2 | 60% | 45 days | 9 | 300 | **33.3** | 3 |
| F4 | Self-booking portal | 510 | 1 | 70% | 12 wks | 12 | 357 | **29.8** | 4 |
| F2 | Route optimisation v2 | 300 | 3 | 50% | 20 wks | 20 | 450 | **22.5** | 5 |

**Committed obligations (outside the RICE ranking)**

| ID | Item | Normalised effort | Why it is not ranked by RICE | Hard date |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| F3 | SAML SSO | 6 | The obligation is contractual. Its RICE score of 5.8 (35 × 1 × 100% ÷ 6) understates the stakes, because $180k ARR is exposed to an exit clause. | Live by 31 Oct 2026 |
| F5 | Map provider migration | 8 | It has no customer-facing Reach or Impact, so it cannot get a RICE score. It avoids a +40% renewal or the loss of maps, and it is a prerequisite for F2. | Done by 31 Dec 2026 |

**How I handled them.** F3 and F5 are reserved first: 14 of 48 weeks. The scored items then compete for the remaining **34 weeks**.

## 2. H2 plan

**Selection logic.** After the commitments, 34 weeks remain. F6 (3) and F1 (16) are clear wins and leave 15 weeks. Two candidates compete for that last slot, and they cannot both fit (9 + 12 = 21 > 15):

- **F7:** higher RICE ratio, value 300.
- **F4:** lower RICE ratio, value 357.

I chose **F4**. The bundle F6 + F1 + F4 delivers **1,299** total value. That is the maximum achievable in 34 weeks. The F7 alternative delivers 1,242, and every bundle containing F2 delivers at most 1,020. Section 4 covers the trade-off.

**Quarter allocation**

| Quarter | Item | Effort (eng-wks) | Sequencing note |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Q3** | F3 SAML SSO | 6 | Starts first. Aim to be live in August, which leaves about 2 months of buffer before 31 Oct. |
| Q3 | F1 Offline mode | 16 | Top churn driver, so it ships as early as possible. |
| **Q3 total** | | **22 / 24** | 2 wks slack held as SSO/F1 contingency |
| **Q4** | F5 Map migration | 8 | Starts first in Q4, targeting completion by mid-November. That leaves about 6 weeks before the contract ends. |
| Q4 | F4 Self-booking portal | 12 | |
| Q4 | F6 Invoice PDF redesign | 3 | Small item, so it can absorb slippage if needed. |
| **Q4 total** | | **23 / 24** | 1 wk slack |
| **H2 total** | | **45 / 48** | 3 wks slack (6%) |

**Why this split.** No item is split across quarters.

- **F3 goes in Q3** so the contractual date is never at risk.
- **F5 goes in Q4 rather than Q3.** Q3 cannot hold F3 + F5 + F1 (30 weeks). Putting F1 in Q4 alongside F5 would also overflow (16 + 8 + 12 > 24). F5's deadline is year-end, so a Q4 start with priority sequencing is acceptable.
- **F6 sits in Q4.** It does not fit in Q3 alongside F3 and F1 (25 weeks).

## 3. Cut list (not in H2)

| ID | Item | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| F2 | Route optimisation v2 | It has the lowest RICE (22.5) and lowest confidence (50%). At 20 weeks it could only fit by displacing F1, the top churn driver. Its prerequisite F5 only lands in Q4, so it becomes the lead candidate for Q1 2027. |
| F7 | Technician skills matching | It lost the last slot to F4 on total value (300 vs 357). Its estimate was submitted in days, so it needs a re-estimate before it is re-planned for Q1 2027. |

## 4. Memo

**To:** Richard Roe (VP Sales), Mary Major (Head of Customer Success)
**Re:** H2 2026 roadmap

Mary, SSO is the first thing the squad builds in Q3. We are targeting go-live in August, which gives us about two months of buffer against Brightwell's 31 October date. The map migration is also locked in and starts first in Q4, so we avoid the 40% renewal uplift.

Richard, I know Route Optimisation v2 is your headline, and I haven't scheduled it for H2. It needs the map migration finished first, which happens in Q4. Fitting its 20 weeks would mean dropping Offline Mode, our top churn-interview request, for an item we currently rate at 50% confidence. The good news is that the migration clears the path, so Route Opt v2 leads the Q1 2027 candidate list.

**The key trade-off** was the last 15 weeks: the self-booking portal versus technician skills matching. Skills matching scores slightly higher per week of effort. The portal, however, delivers more total value to more accounts (510 vs 250), and its estimate is more reliable. I chose the portal.

**What would change my mind:**
- **Route Opt v2:** if Sales can show evidence, such as signed or late-stage enterprise deals contingent on it, that lifts its confidence to about 80% or more. At that point a plan built around it beats this one. We would then revisit Q4 once the migration is done.
- **Skills matching:** if the re-estimate comes in materially below 9 weeks, or its reach grows.
- **Either commitment slipping:** SSO or the migration slipping would consume our 3 weeks of slack first. The invoice redesign is the first item I would cut to protect them.
